archetypes.name: dependency-verify-first
archetypes.rationale: The plan has at least eight 'verify-first' clauses gating on PR #3548 landing, but does not specify concretely which file lines to read or what the success/failure branches look like — gaps that can cause an implementer to skip or repeat work incorrectly.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every 'verify-first' clause in the plan against the named scope files. For each clause, check whether the plan specifies (a) which file/line to read to determine if the surface already exists, (b) exactly what code shape counts as 'present', and (c) what to do when absent. Flag any verify-first that lacks a concrete read target or leaves the implementer guessing. Cross-check the stated hard dependency on PR #3548: does the plan correctly identify which surfaces #3548 owns vs. which are net-new here, and could any described edit overlap with (or duplicate) a #3548 change? Also verify that the plan's list of files to modify is internally consistent — no file mentioned in the approach section that is absent from the named file list, and no file named but left undescribed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: env-var-propagation
archetypes.rationale: The plan threads SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE through tally, loop, run-step3-review, SKILL.md re-tally, and two result-env files, with explicit input/output variable split rules — making contract consistency across all these surfaces the primary defect risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace every described occurrence of SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE (and the _STAGED_SCOPE_ANCHOR vs _PARSED_SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE split) through the plan's proposed changes to assess-plan-round.sh, tally-plan-review.sh, plan-review-loop.sh, run-step3-review.sh, and SKILL.md. For each script, verify the plan specifies the correct emit terminal (ok and main-agent-vote-required only; omit on tally-error) and that the input variable is never used as the persist variable. Check that both result env files (.step3-plan-review-result.env and .step3-review-result.env) are named consistently for re-tally refresh. Identify any path where the plan describes emitting or propagating the KV inconsistently with the stated contract (FINDING_7, FINDING_8, FINDING_12). Also check whether the plan's stale-seed test scenarios cover all the described propagation paths or leave a relay surface untested. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: security-doc-accuracy
archetypes.rationale: The plan's SECURITY.md addition claims a two-surface trust model (inline renderers vs path-only handoffs) and distinguishes staged-anchor vs legacy-fallback provenance — accuracy failures here produce false assurance rather than actual coverage.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check the proposed SECURITY.md 'Plan-review scope-anchor pipeline' section against the plan's code descriptions for render-assessor-prompt.sh, revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh, and launch-claude-subprocess.sh. Verify that the two stated surfaces (inline renderers and path-only KV handoffs) match what the plan actually describes each script doing — look for cases where the doc claims a surface is covered but the corresponding code description still uses a legacy fallback or raw sed path. Check whether the assessor legacy-fallback note is consistent with the assess-plan-round.sh resolution order change (staged anchor first, then legacy). Flag any place where SECURITY.md would overstate coverage (e.g. claiming assessor coverage before the assessor feature-block render is hardened) or conflate staged-anchor provenance with source-specific inline inputs. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
